title: 1992 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Let \(i=\sqrt{-1}.\) For \(n\ge1,\) define a sequence of complex numbers by \[ \begin{aligned} z_1&=0,\\ z_{n+1}&=z_n^2+i. \end{aligned} \] In the complex plane, how far from the origin is \(z_{111}?\)

solutions.text:
The first terms are \[ \begin{aligned} z_1&=0,\quad z_2=i,\quad z_3=-1+i,\\ z_4&=-i,\quad z_5=-1+i. \end{aligned} \] Hence the sequence alternates between \(-1+i\) at odd indices and \(-i\) at even indices from \(z_3\) onward. Therefore \(z_{111}=-1+i,\) whose distance from the origin is \(\sqrt{(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt2.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Compute the first few terms rather than trying to expand \(z_{111}\)
Look for a cycle beginning with \(z_3\)
